title: Menu Placement Strategy
description: Explains flip and clamp placement algorithm.
body: Flip, then clamp. A menu that does not fit to the right of the pointer is drawn to its left rather than slid left until it fits — sliding leaves the pointer sitting on top of the menu's own rows, and the first click after the one that opened it lands on whichever row happened to slide under the cursor. Flipping keeps the corner at the pointer, which is what every desktop menu does.
